description: macOS system speech as a TTS engine on the OpenAI door: POST /v1/audio/speech with model='say' (or say:<voice>/say:<locale>/say:<voice>:<locale>) renders through the `say` command - no model, no GPU, voices are the ones the owner's accessibility setup already sounds like. Long replies are rendered in sentence-sized pieces, spooled to disk and stitched (memory tracks the longest piece, not the longest answer; non-WAV formats transcode block-wise from the spool), and stream=true sends each piece as it finishes (first audio at 1.3 s of a 63.9 s answer, measured). The per-reply audio ceiling is the OMLX_SAY_MAX_AUDIO_MB environment (default 256 MB): text that cannot fit even at the fastest speaking pace is refused BEFORE rendering, never cut short. Ships the Settings > Integrations card (engine switch, per-language voice pins, long-input policy, segment size), the voice roster endpoint, 10 locales, and two test files. Vendored from the zviratko/omlx feat/tts-macos-say branch (rebased onto 18fe1c38); upstream PR https://github.com/jundot/omlx/pull/4952 is open - on merge, link the PR source and drop this vendored copy.
